hero.title: CTX Frame
hero.description: The intentional context layer between product thinking and AI-generated code.

thesis.quote: AI can already read your code. The problem is what the code doesn't contain.

gap.title: Code documents the what. Never the why.

items.title: Why this module has this boundary
Why this flow was designed this way
items.body: and not the more obvious one

gap.halfMap: The AI operates with half the map. It can read the implementation. It cannot read the intent.

problem.title: The AI doesn't improvise badly. It improvises reasonably well.
problem.subtitle: And that's exactly the problem.
problem.body: When intentional context is missing, the model does what looks technically correct. Most of the time, the code works. It passes tests. It looks good in the diff.
lines: But it might be violating a business constraint nobody wrote down anywhere.
It might be coupling two domains that must remain separated.
It might be making the most obvious design decision — which was rejected eight months ago for a reason only three people remember.
problem.conclusion: The problem isn't that the AI generates bad code. It's that it generates code that cannot know if it's correct.

cdd.title: Context-Driven Development
cdd.subtitle: When intentional context exists as a first-class artifact, something deeper than AI output quality changes. The order in which development happens changes.
cdd.insight: Code stops being the primary interface of the system. Intentional context is.

pillars.title: Intent before code
pillars.body: The engineer edits the context file. Defines the new behavior, its restrictions, its contracts. The AI doesn't act until the intent is written.

pillars.title: Visible impact before acting
pillars.body: Dependencies are explicit in the context. If a change affects another module, that's visible before a single line of code is written. Not discovered in production.

pillars.title: Correct by construction
pillars.body: The AI operates within the context's guardrails. Product constraints aren't inferred from code — they're written. They can't be accidentally ignored.

demo.title: Edit the context. The code follows.
demo.subtitle: Each scenario shows how a change in intentional context drives a corresponding change in the generated code.

scenarios.label: Base module
scenarios.description: A clean module with no guardrails defined yet. The AI generates minimal, direct code.

scenarios.label: + KYC guardrail
scenarios.description: Add a compliance guardrail. The AI wraps the entire flow in the required verification — without being asked explicitly in a prompt.

scenarios.label: + Scope boundary
scenarios.description: Define ownership boundaries. The AI respects the module's scope and delegates correctly to the compliance module.

scenarios.label: Feature with body
scenarios.description: A complete feature context file: YAML frontmatter + markdown body with flows and an @ pointer. The AI follows the flow structure, not just the guardrails.

scenarios.label: Spec — exact algorithm
scenarios.description: A spec context narrows to a precise implementation detail. The AI preserves exact thresholds, invariants, and order defined in the body — without being asked in a prompt.

hierarchy.title: The hierarchy of intent.
hierarchy.subtitle: Not all intent operates at the same scale. Each level answers different questions and is independently readable.

levels.name: Application
levels.desc: Why the product exists. Global principles, architecture constraints, behavior the model can and cannot modify.
levels.question: Why does this system exist?

levels.name: Capability
levels.desc: A cross-cutting domain shared by multiple modules. Its boundaries, invariants, access restrictions.
levels.question: What domain does this change belong to?

levels.name: Module
levels.desc: What this domain owns, what it doesn't own, and why that boundary exists. Explicit ownership.
levels.question: What belongs to this module and what doesn't?

levels.name: Feature
levels.desc: The concrete behavior: purpose, flows, input/output contracts, non-negotiable guardrails.
levels.question: What problem does it solve and how?

levels.name: Spec
levels.desc: The exact technical detail that must not be lost in any refactoring. Sequences, algorithms, invariants.
levels.question: What precision must be preserved?

notDocs.title: Not documentation. Executable intent.
notDocs.body: Documentation describes what already exists. Intentional context defines what must always be true — regardless of how the implementation evolves.

docs.label: Technical documentation
docs.title: Describes what was built
docs.body: Lives in wikis, READMEs, and comments. Written after the code. Ages with every refactor. No contract — it can say anything.

ctx.label: CTX Frame intentional context
ctx.title: Defines what must always be true
ctx.body: Lives in the repository alongside the code. Written before the code. Doesn't change with refactors — changes when intent changes. Strict contract — AI can validate and respect it.

closing.body: Every system I've built hit the same wall: technically sound code that violated product decisions nobody thought to write down. CTX Frame is my answer to that wall.
